II22A-01.note: Calder (salt, quiet) below Ellery (noise, no salt) dissociates the factors against noise. B (Brenlow vs Ashby) is confounded and strikable by a factorial-savvy student; A and D support noise and tempt a direction-flip.

II22A-02.note: Cassel vs Fairlie holds sun constant and varies fungi. D (Ardel vs Cassel) tempts because Ardel is the 'beneath adults' plot, but it isolates shade and supports Ebbert.

II22A-03.note: Bypass (traffic, no lamps) earlier than lit lanes (lamps, quiet) weakens the lamp hypothesis. A and C support Fairweather and tempt a direction error; B is confounded (downtown has both factors).

II22A-04.note: R-07: +8 min and 55 in salt. C (R-8) is most tempting, passing the temperature test and failing salt at 70; D's 90 is strikable on sight.

II22A-05.note: 35/64 is the only ratio above one-half. Avelin 44/90 is the near-miss; Fallow 15/40 is strikable on sight.

II22A-06.note: Carrick (1,800 m) 6.4 vs Bramley (2,200 m) 6.0 is the dip. D also names Bramley but shows it higher than a lower site; B and C show the normal rise and are strikable once the dip is found by scanning the column.

II22B-01.note: North cliff July (rain, no freeze-thaw) beating March (freeze-thaw) weakens Grieg. Pattern: C is the only option in which the July/rain month is the larger, so a student who maps July=rain can pick it without tracking the cliffs.

II22B-02.note: Sealed wool (wool gas trapped, city air excluded) beating ventilated cotton (city air only) pits the two sources against each other. The key varies two factors at once, so a student trained to strike confounded pairs may wrongly strike it; C is the opposite-condition pair and the hardest to dismiss.

II22B-03.note: Iselund eruptions rose from 2000-03 to 2005-08 (both normal-rain years, pumping begins between) against Lark. C is tempting as a Kalvnesby control but shows an increase where pumping does not reach, which says nothing against Lark; B mixes drought and field and is strikable.

II22B-04.note: Garvik (64 m) is the deepest lake, and Hesk lost 27 days vs Garvik's 19. Every option is accurate and every comparison lake lost fewer days than Hesk, so only the depth column discriminates; Lunmar/Ivren tempt by size of loss.

II22B-05.note: Ivarsby is the only young-sediment well over 100 m. Gavlin (young, highest arsenic) tempts but is 45 m deep; Haldor tempts as deep and over 10 but draws old sediment.

II22B-06.note: Joskar (51 km) thicker than Ilvikmoen (38 km). B, C, D all show the normal thinning and fall away once the student checks which site is farther; the one non-monotone pair in the column is visible on a scan.

II22C-01.note: Nolvaston (breakfast, no tardiness change) beating Rossmere isolates breakfast. A (Mendrick vs Rossmere) is the most tempting but is confounded; C actually supports Okafor.

II22C-02.note: Pruett (radio only) above Nantle (contact only) weakens face-to-face. A (Mossbury vs Ombry) is confounded; B and C support Paredes and catch direction errors.

II22C-03.note: Floor 4 is the only lottery floor with real daylight. D (floor 3, lottery but blank wall) is the most tempting for a student who tracks only the seniority confound; C (floor 2) has daylight but seniority seating.

II22C-04.note: Nuskirk 7/30 = 23% is the only drop above 20%. A (Orvel, largest absolute drop of 11) is the designed absolute-vs-relative trap; the other ratios cluster at 16-18%, so arithmetic is required.

II22C-05.note: Medlow: 40% cards, 45 shoppers per vendor. Options omit the card column, so students must bring in a third cell; C (Ossiter, 35% cards) passes the card test but has only 35 per vendor, and B (Rushmere, 42 per vendor) passes the ratio but not the card test.

II22C-06.note: Quist (70 mi) at 66 below Pirrock (57 mi) at 72. D names Quist but against a nearer, cheaper town; A and C show the normal rise and fall away once the single price inversion in the column is spotted.

II22D-01.note: Wrennick vs Skarra holds fees constant (none) and varies stream type. B (Thrane vs Skarra) is the tempting confounded pair; A isolates fees and supports Sorensen.

II22D-02.note: Ulving (pine, damp stone) above Tamm (oak, dry timber) dissociates damp from oak. C (Selander vs Vass) is confounded; B and D hold church type constant and support Wennberg.

II22D-03.note: Tolvik (river) vs Saltrup (hills), same decade after 1735, isolates glass access. B is the tempting river-over-hill option but compares across decades straddling both 1720 and 1735; D is the only same-decade river/hill comparison.

II22D-04.note: Tarrow 60/96 = 0.625; every other mill is ~0.70. D (Yarrel, largest absolute saving of 45) is the magnitude trap; the 0.70 cluster requires arithmetic, though the key's uniquely different ratio may stand out to a student who checks one.

II22D-05.note: 1500s-1510s: paper flat at 19, books 6.0 to 5.1. B is the strongest trap (paper flat at 25, but books rose); A and C have falling paper. Options omit the paper column, so two columns must be combined.

II22D-06.note: Sollen: 1.45 s, 5,440/640 = 8.5 m3 per seat. Teverin and Wrayne pass reverberation but fall to 7.5 per seat, requiring division; Ulmar is strikable on reverberation alone.
